Theorem
[Uniqueness, energy method]

1. ch2:2.3-thm-10\group Energy Methods For $g\in C(\Gamma _T)$ and $f\in C(U_T)$, there is at most one $u\in C_1^2(\overline U_T)$ satisfying \[ u_t-\Delta u=f\ \text{in }U_T, \qquad u=g\ \text{on }\Gamma _T. \]
Proof

↗ lem:uniqueness-heat-bounded-domain-anisotropic \sketch For the difference $w$ of two solutions, define $e(t)=\int _Uw(x,t)^2\, dx$. Since $w=0$ on the parabolic boundary,

\[ e'(t)=2\int _Uw\Delta w\, dx=-2\int _U|Dw|^2\, dx\le 0. \]

As $e(0)=0$, one has $w=0$.

□
